source.title: Captured by Captions: On Memorization and its Mitigation in CLIP Models
source.authors: Wen-Hao Wang; Adam Dziedzic; Grace C. Kim; Michael Backes; Franziska Boenisch

page_placements.theme: Example selection and sampling have conditional effects

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how removing high-memorization samples affects downstream performance in CLIP models, extending the removal finding to a different model family and training setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports memorization scores, text and image augmentation results, and model-size comparisons. These do not test the listed claim versions about natural-label generalization in the specified architectures and recipes. Removal-curve values are shown in figures; the text describes trends and cutoffs but does not give exact accuracy values for individual removal counts.
record.test_reason: The removal experiments address a related question, but do not measure V8's defined behavior. CLIPMem ranks examples by their inclusion's effect on image–text alignment, rather than on correct prediction of their own labels; the outcome is downstream ImageNet linear-probing accuracy. The supervised appendix experiment deliberately introduces label errors and also evaluates transferred representations. Neither establishes a test of the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the removal experiments. The authors conclude more broadly that text-focused interventions can reduce CLIP memorization while improving downstream generalization. They hypothesize that initial removal gains reflect eliminating mis-captioned examples, whereas later losses reflect removing useful atypical examples; the appendix provides supporting experiments rather than definitive attribution.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CLIP contrastive pretraining and CLIPMem-based sample selection, then evaluates ImageNet linear-probing accuracy; the version describes ResNet-50 supervised classification and test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: The removal effect changes with the number of samples removed and differs by training dataset: the stated cutoff is between 400 and 800 for COCO and between 1600 and 3200 for CC3M.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing high-CLIPMem examples initially improves ImageNet linear-probing accuracy relative to random removal, then becomes worse after crossovers bracketed by 400–800 removals on COCO and 1600–3200 on CC3M.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing examples with high inclusion-dependent image–text alignment can improve CLIP transfer accuracy initially, while larger removals can harm it more than random removal.

fits_no_version.finding: With five COCO captions, the removal experiment shows the same qualitative pattern, with a performance peak at roughly 500 removals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The initial transfer benefit from removing high-CLIPMem examples also occurs with multiple captions, and its peak depends on the caption setup.

fits_no_version.finding: A supervised ViT-tiny trained on CIFAR-10 with 200 deliberately flipped labels shows an initial ImageNet linear-probing improvement after memorization-based removal, peaking near 200 removals; the comparison crosses random removal near 3200.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In deliberately label-corrupted supervised training, memorization-based filtering can initially improve downstream representation utility.

fits_no_version.finding: Balanced multiple captions and suitably scaled text-embedding noise reduce CLIPMem while improving downstream accuracy; stronger noise eventually lowers accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some text-domain training changes improve CLIP transfer accuracy while reducing alignment-based memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: ViT-Large has higher average CLIPMem and ImageNet linear-probing accuracy than ViT-Base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater model size can coexist with higher alignment-based memorization and better transfer accuracy in CLIP.

record.problems: The removal-curve results are presented in figures; the text gives qualitative trends and cutoff ranges, not exact accuracy values at the reported removal counts. The downstream measure is ImageNet linear-probing accuracy, and the tested models are CLIP rather than the supervised ResNet-50 specified in V8.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 and Table 8 report text-augmentation and embedding-noise results, while Table 5 reports model-size results. These do not test a listed version's defined behavior. Figure 6 shows further removal counts, but the text gives only the initial trend and cutoff ranges; individual figure-only points were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: No comparison of near-perfect random-label fitting with held-out accuracy under natural and random labels. Shuffled-caption alignment scores do not establish these outcomes.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or test of local connectivity.
No controlled optimizer comparison under limited or broader tuning.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or rankings of generalization gaps.

No qualifying comparison of removing examples ranked by their inclusion's effect on correct own-label prediction and measuring classifier test accuracy. CLIP removal uses alignment-based memorization and downstream transfer accuracy; the supervised appendix introduces label corruption deliberately.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied prose supports the qualitative removal trends, but exact curve values cannot be recovered from the extracted figure text. These findings do not challenge or support V8 as defined merely because both experiments remove examples described as memorized.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Does not sweep width or test error past an interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected classifiers.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on the listed benchmarks.
Does not study batch-size generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare sharpness measures.
Tests CLIP models trained on COCO and CC3M, not ResNet-50 on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet. Reports ImageNet linear-probing accuracy rather than the specified classifier test accuracy.

rows.subject: CLIP model trained on COCO
rows.operation_detail: Retrained after removing up to 100 samples selected by highest CLIPMem; compared with random removal.
rows.measure: ImageNet linear-probing accuracy; exact value not stated in text
rows.baseline: Random sample removal; exact value not stated in text
rows.value: CLIPMem-based removal gives a sharp increase in downstream performance in comparison to removing random samples; exact value not stated in text
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the change but supplies no exact accuracy values for this range.
rows.check: The reported initial improvement is supported by Section 4.6, but CLIPMem-based removal does not measure V8's label-prediction-based memorization. Preserve the qualitative finding without assigning it a V8 state.

rows.subject: CLIP model trained on COCO
rows.operation_detail: Retrained after removing progressively more samples selected by highest CLIPMem; compared with random removal.
rows.measure: ImageNet linear-probing accuracy; exact value not stated in text
rows.baseline: Random sample removal; exact value not stated in text
rows.value: At the cutoff between 400 and 800 removed samples, performance becomes worse when removing by highest memorization instead of randomly; exact value not stated in text
rows.note: Text states the cutoff range and direction; individual curve values are figure-only.
rows.check: CLIPMem and downstream linear probing do not establish V8's effect. Also, 400–800 removals brackets the crossover; performance is worse after crossing it, not necessarily throughout this interval.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study discusses supervised memorization and generalization and compares its findings with prior work, but its CLIP removal experiments do not measure V8's defined behavior.

tranche.reason: CLIPMem measures inclusion-dependent image–text alignment, rather than V8's inclusion-dependent correct-label prediction. The removal results concern a related construct and downstream ImageNet linear probing, so they fit no listed version.

source_check.notes: The removal intervals bracket crossovers; worse-than-random performance applies after crossing them. Exact removal-curve accuracies are not stated in the prose; cannot_determine refers to the claim version, not uncertainty about the reported qualitative trends.
